claims.claim_text: Federal Solutions segment generated $3.22B revenue in FY2025 (51% of $6.36B total), with the U.S. federal government and its agencies representing 'substantially all' of the segment's revenue. Customers include the Intelligence Community and the Departments of War, Energy, State, Homeland Security, and Commerce, plus NASA and FAA.

One customer set within the U.S. federal government represented over 20% of total Parsons revenue in FY2025; the second-year option for a large 'confidential contract' in Federal Solutions was significantly reduced during 2025 and is currently winding down. Awards from that confidential contract fell from $1.5B in FY2024 to $293M in FY2025.

Parsons supports the Golden Dome homeland-defense program (ground- and space-based capabilities to defend the U.S. against missile, drone, and threat-based attacks) through its MDA TEAMS Next program and Non-Kinetics Effects (NKE) capabilities, positioning it for forward Pentagon spending growth.

Parsons has been providing support to the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) for nearly 40 years with approximately 1,000 personnel embedded with the customer. The MDA TEAMS Next program is described as the Federal Solutions vehicle through which Parsons participates in MDA work, including Golden Dome.

BlackSignal Technologies (acquired Aug 2024, $203.7M) added counterspace radio frequency, electronic warfare, and cyber capabilities — described as 'markets anticipated to grow more than 10% annually with double-digit margin expectations.' Acquisition expanded Parsons' customer base across the Department of War and Intelligence Community.

Over 4,400 of Parsons' skilled workforce hold government security clearances (out of ~10,600 employees with degrees and 3,600+ with advanced degrees, per Human Capital section). Cleared workforce is the basis for Federal Solutions delivery on cyber, classified, and IC programs.

Total backlog as of Dec 31, 2025 was $8.7B ($6.4B funded, $2.3B unfunded), DOWN 2% YoY from $8.9B at Dec 31, 2024. Federal Solutions backlog declined to $4.15B (implied) from $4.67B prior year; book-to-bill was 1.0 in FY2025 vs 1.1 in FY2023. Awards in Federal Solutions fell primarily due to delay in timing of contract awards and reduced confidential-contract activity.

Parsons' Federal Solutions Defense & Intelligence customer set includes U.S. Department of War (DoD), U.S. Intelligence Community, Department of Commerce, NOAA, MDA, U.S. Air Force, NASA; Critical Infrastructure customers include DHS, USACE, FAA, DOS, DOE, DTRA, USPS, DOL. The U.S. federal government represented ~$4.7B of $5.18B North America revenue (~91% of NA, 74% of total) in FY2025.
